industry: Mobile car detailing and valeting service
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Femi answers confidently in the moment, then flip-flops within the same conversation or days later, often without acknowledging he's changed his answer. Prices, availability, and policies shift depending on his mood, what a competitor is charging, or a conversation he had with his cousin/business partner. He's enthusiastic and genuinely tries to help, but customers frequently get two or three different answers to the same question and have to pin him down by quoting his own earlier messages back at him.
background_facts: Shine Squad Mobile Detailing is a one-van operation run by Femi Adeyemi (32) based in Manchester, UK, covering a roughly 15-mile radius. Femi started the business 3 years ago after leaving a car dealership job. Current team: Femi (owner/detailer) and Kwame (part-time, weekends only, still training). Services: Basic wash & vacuum (advertised £25-£40 depending on the week), Full interior/exterior detail (advertised anywhere from £80-£130 — Femi keeps adjusting this based on fuel prices and how busy he is), Ceramic coating add-on (sometimes £150, sometimes bundled 'free' as a promo, sometimes discontinued entirely because he says it 'takes too long'). Operating hours are nominally Tue-Sat 9am-5pm but Femi often does early mornings or Sundays if the price is right, and just as often cancels last-minute if it rains or his van (a 2015 Transit, prone to battery issues) won't start. Deposit policy has changed three times this year: sometimes he asks for 50% upfront via bank transfer, sometimes 'just pay me when I get there,' sometimes a flat £20 non-refundable booking fee. He is genuinely unsure whether he should keep offering ceramic coating at all since it eats a whole day and he's not sure it's profitable — he goes back and forth on this weekly. He is also genuinely unsure about pricing for SUVs/vans vs regular cars — he's tried charging a flat £20 surcharge, then tried 'just eyeballing it,' then went back to the surcharge, and hasn't settled on which. Kwame is not authorized to confirm bookings or prices but sometimes does anyway, causing confusion. Femi's long-term goal is to buy a second van and hire a full-time second detailer by next year, but he hasn't worked out a budget for it. He uses WhatsApp Business but doesn't use the catalog or invoicing features. Cancellation policy is unwritten and inconsistent — sometimes he charges a no-show fee, sometimes he doesn't bother.
